property: Shared-medium random access and collision/retransmission problem framing were part of the documented intellectual ancestry of Ethernet; Ethernet then added carrier sensing, collision detection and its own coaxial physical/interface engineering.

date_or_range.notes: ALOHA work predates the PARC Ethernet design and the 1976 Metcalfe/Boggs publication documents the relationship.

sources.locator: Metcalfe & Boggs, Ethernet: Distributed Packet Switching for Local Computer Networks, historical/design discussion
sources.notes: Use exact page/paragraph locator when the canonical scan is registered.
Contextual support for what ALOHA itself actually was.

negative_claims: This edge does not claim that Ethernet copied ALOHAnet packet formats, radio hardware or retransmission procedure unchanged.
This edge does not make experimental Ethernet equivalent to later 10 Mbit/s DIX or IEEE 802.3 Ethernet.
open_questions: Promote the 1973 and 1974 PARC memos into source records and locate the earliest explicit ALOHA citations.
Separate Pure ALOHA versus Slotted ALOHA influence claims by document.
notes: Example of a legitimate influence edge where documentary evidence exists and the inherited property is narrowly stated.
